Prepared inputs for scale estimation

Source: R/doc_fit_class.R
multiScaleR_data-class.Rd

kernel_prep() and kernel_prep_by_group() return an object of class "multiScaleR_data", a list that holds everything the fitting functions need about the survey points and the raster cells around them. Pass it as kernel_inputs to multiScale_optim(), multiScale_bayes(), cross_validate(), and related functions. This page describes every element.

Elements

  • kernel_dat: data frame of the initial kernel-weighted covariate values, centered and scaled to unit variance, with one row per point and one column per covariate. Row names match the row names of pts or are sequential integers. Fit your starting model to these columns.

  • d_list: named list, one element per point, of distances from the point to every raster cell within the buffer. NULL in lean mode.

  • raw_cov: named list, one element per point, of matrices holding the raw raster cell values within the buffer, aligned with d_list. Each is stored as a dense or sparse matrix, whichever is smaller. NULL in lean mode.

  • kernel: the kernel name ("gaussian", "exp", "expow", or "fixed").

  • sigma: initial sigma values on the internal scale (map units divided by unit_conv).

  • shape: initial shape values for "expow", otherwise NULL.

  • min_D: approximate minimum distance between cells, used as the lower bound for sigma during the search, in map units.

  • max_D: the max_D you supplied, the upper bound for sigma, in map units.

  • n_covs: number of covariates whose scale is estimated.

  • unit_conv: internal distance scaling factor, equal to max_D.

  • scale_vars: data frame of class "multiScaleR_vars" describing every covariate specification (see msr_vars()).

  • resolution: raster cell resolution in map units.

  • cell_size: cell width and height in map units. Cross-validation uses them to keep intersecting cells whose centers lie beyond max_D.

  • n_cols: number of raster columns, used by adjacency-based landscape metrics.

  • binned: when bin = TRUE, a list of distance-binned summaries (representative bin distances and value and count matrices for each covariate) that speed up the search. NULL when bin = FALSE or when no covariate is a kernel-weighted mean.

  • surface_binned: when bin = TRUE, linearly binned power sums for kernel-weighted surface metrics (surface_var(weighted = TRUE) with "sq", "ssk", or "sku") that speed up the refit search. Each cell's centered value powers are split between the two nearest distance nodes. NULL when bin = FALSE, when kernel = "fixed", or when no covariate is such a metric. The cell-level data stay stored.

  • cell_data_stored: FALSE only in lean mode (store_cell_data = FALSE), when d_list and raw_cov were dropped.

  • scl_params: named list with mean and sd, the centering and scaling values applied to kernel_dat.

  • raster_group: from kernel_prep_by_group() only, the raster group of each point.

Lean mode keeps only the binned summaries. It works only when every covariate is a kernel-weighted mean, because landscape and surface metrics need the cell-level data. Printing the object reports the number of points and covariates, the kernel, the binning, and the distance bounds.

See also

kernel_prep(), kernel_prep_by_group(), msr_vars(), multiScaleR, and vignette("v02-user-guide", package = "multiScaleR").

Examples

data(pts)
hab <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "hab.tif",
                               package = "multiScaleR"))
inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = hab, max_D = 250,
                      kernel = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE)
inputs                    # short summary of the prepared inputs
#> 
#> There are 75 observations at 1 spatial covariate(s): 
#> hab
#> 
#> The specified kernel is:
#> gaussian
#> 
#> Number of elements: 
#> 2052
#> Distance binning:
#> enabled (256 distance bins per covariate)
#> Minimum Distance:
#> 10
#> Maximum Distance:
#> 250
#> Unit Conversion:
#> 250
head(inputs$kernel_dat)   # standardized covariate values at the start
#>          hab
#> 1 -0.4206979
#> 2  1.7520402
#> 3  0.5073754
#> 4 -0.8959421
#> 5 -0.1734359
#> 6  0.8108489
inputs$max_D              # upper bound for sigma, in map units
#> [1] 250
